name: British Citizenship Test 1
questions: What are two responsibilities that you will have as a British citizen or permanent resident of the UK?
To look after the area in which you live and the environment
To look after yourself and your family
To stay in the UK forever
To promote work in your local community
To look after the area in which you live and the environment; To look after yourself and your family
Citizens and permanent residents of the UK are expected to respect and obey the law, look after themselves and their family, and look after the local area and environment.
Big Ben is the nickname for the Great Bell of the clock at the north end of the Palace of Westminster (the Houses of Parliament).
When were men and women given the right to vote at the age of 21?
In 1918, women over 30 and men over 21 achieved the vote. In 1928, voting rights were equalized, granting both men and women the right to vote at the age of 21.
Where is the UK geographically located?
The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland is geographically located in the north-west of the European continent.
Who is the patron Saint of Scotland?
St Andrew is Scotland's patron saint. St George represents England, St David represents Wales, and St Patrick represents Northern Ireland.
Which two houses fought in the Wars of the Roses?
The House of York; The House of Lancaster
The Wars of the Roses (1455-1485) was fought between the House of Lancaster (red rose) and the House of York (white rose) for the English crown.
The Bill of Rights of 1689 confirmed the right to vote for all adult men.
The Bill of Rights of 1689 confirmed parliamentary supremacy but did not grant voting rights to all adult men, which only came after the Reform Acts of the 19th and 20th centuries.
The Cenotaph, designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens, is a prominent war memorial located in Whitehall, London, hosting the annual Remembrance Day service.
Who was the first female Prime Minister of the UK?
Margaret Thatcher was the first female Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, serving from 1979 to 1990.
Who chairs the debates at the House of Commons?
The Speaker is an MP elected by fellow MPs to chair debates and keep order in the House of Commons chamber.
Who was the captain of the English football team that won the World Cup in 1966?
Bobby Moore was the legendary captain of the England football squad that triumphed in the 1966 World Cup final against West Germany.
When did the English defeat the Spanish Armada?
In 1588, during the reign of Queen Elizabeth I, England successfully repelled the massive invasion fleet sent by Spain, known as the Spanish Armada.
Anyone can make a complaint about the police by writing to the Chief Constable of the police force involved.
If someone wishes to complain about police treatment, they can do so by contacting the Chief Constable of the police force directly.
What is the minimum age required to serve on a jury?
To serve on a jury in England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland, you must be between 18 and 75 years old.
Jury service is an essential civic duty. Individuals are selected randomly by a computer from the local electoral register.
A public holiday when banks are open all day
A public holiday for people working in banks
An additional day off that every worker in the UK is entitled to
A public holiday when banks and many other businesses are closed for the day
A public holiday when banks and many other businesses are closed for the day
Bank holidays are official public holidays where commercial banks and many retail/business operations close for the day.
What will you be given to vote before a general election takes place?
Before an election, registered voters receive a official poll card showing their designated polling station and date/hours.
Which of the following statements is correct?
Solicitors’ charges are usually based on how much time they spend on a case
Solicitors’ charges are usually based on the nature of a case and its importance
Solicitors’ charges are usually based on how much time they spend on a case
Solicitors charge fees usually based on the hourly rate and time spent compiling records, researching law, or preparing defenses.
By law, which TWO types of media have to give a balanced coverage of all political parties and equal time to rival viewpoints before an election?
Under broadcasting law, both TV and radio broadcasters must strictly maintain political balance, unlike printed newspapers.
Which of the following territories is a Crown dependency but is NOT part of the UK?
The Channel Islands (Jersey and Guernsey) and the Isle of Man are Crown dependencies, which have self-governance and are not officially part of the United Kingdom.
What did Sir Frank Whittle invent in the 1930s?
Frank Whittle, a British Royal Air Force officer, is famously credited with inventing and developing the jet propulsion engine during the 1930s.
William Wordsworth was an English Romantic poet famously associated with the Lake District, who wrote the iconic poem 'I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud' (commonly known as 'The Daffodils').
Who was given the title of Lord Protector?
Following the execution of King Charles I in 1649, England briefly became a republic. Oliver Cromwell became the leader of the country as Lord Protector.
What are the 40 days before Easter called?
Lent refers to the 40 days before Easter, representing a period of reflection, fasting, and spiritual preparation in the Christian calendar.

name: British Citizenship Test 2
questions: What is the Home Secretary responsible for?
The Home Secretary is responsible for policing, national security, counter-terrorism, and immigration policy in the UK.
St Helena is a British overseas territory and it is part of the United Kingdom.
St Helena is a British overseas territory but is not part of the United Kingdom.
Several Church of England bishops sit in the House of Lords.
Senior bishops of the Church of England sit in the House of Lords as 'Lords Spiritual'.
When walking your dog in a public place, you must ensure:
That your dog does not play with other dogs
That your dog wears a collar showing the name and address of the owner
That your dog wears a high visibility jacket
That your dog does not bark
That your dog wears a collar showing the name and address of the owner
By law, dogs in public places must wear a collar with the name and address of the owner inscribed on it or on a plate/tag.
Women over the age of 30 were given the right to vote as a result of their contribution towards the war effort. Which war was that?
Due to women's outstanding contribution during the First World War, the Representation of the People Act 1918 gave women over 30 the right to vote.
When did Ireland become a republic?
In 1949, Ireland officially left the Commonwealth and declared itself a republic, ending remaining constitutional links to Britain.
Where did the first farmers come from?
The first farmers arrived in Britain about 6,000 years ago from south-east Europe, bringing crops, cattle, and pottery.
Who was an important contributor to the ‘pop art’ movement of the 1960’s?
David Hockney was a major and highly influential contributor to the 'pop art' movement of the 1960s.
Who became Prime Minister and was an inspirational leader to the British people during WWII?
Winston Churchill was appointed Prime Minister in 1940 and served as Britain's charismatic and historic wartime leader throughout WWII.
Who led the first invasion of Britain?
In 55 BC, Roman general Julius Caesar led the first Roman invasion attempt on Britain, although the full conquest began later in 43 AD.
Under which king did the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms in England unite to defeat the Vikings?
King Alfred the Great of Wessex defeated the Viking invaders and began the unification of the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms under one monarch.
When was the Magna Carta created?
The Magna Carta was signed by King John in 1215, establishing the legal principle that even the monarch is subject to the rule of law.
Northern Ireland has its own banknotes, which are valid everywhere in the UK.
Northern Ireland banks issue their own currency notes, which are legal banknotes valid for transactions throughout the United Kingdom.
Which of the following plays was written by William Shakespeare?
A Midsummer Night's Dream is a romantic comedy written by William Shakespeare in the late 16th century.
How many members does a jury have in England, Wales and Northern Ireland?
In England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, a criminal jury consists of 12 people. In Scotland, a jury is made up of 15 members.
Which two of the following religious communities celebrate Diwali?
Diwali (the Festival of Lights) is celebrated widely by Hindu, Sikh, and Jain communities in the autumn.
The day when Jesus Christ rose from the dead
The day when Jesus Christ was born
The day when Jesus Christ died
The day when Jesus Christ became 30 years old
The day when Jesus Christ died
Good Friday commemorates the crucifixion of Jesus Christ, while Easter Sunday celebrates his resurrection.
St Patrick’s day is a public holiday in Northern Ireland.
St Patrick's Day (17th March) is a designated public/bank holiday in Northern Ireland.
Which was the last successful foreign invasion of England that took place in 1066?
The Norman Conquest, led by William the Conqueror in 1066 after defeating King Harold at Hastings, was the last successful foreign invasion of England.
Where are the Crown Jewels kept?
The priceless Crown Jewels, still used in royal coronations today, are kept safely inside the Jewel House in the historic Tower of London.
Which sport can be traced back to the 15th century in Scotland?
Golf has deep historical roots in Scotland and its modern game layout can be traced back to 15th-century Scottish play.
Who was the first person in England to print books using a printing press?
William Caxton was the first English printer, establishing a printing press in Westminster in 1476 to reproduce historic texts.
Which court deals with minor criminal cases in England, Wales and Northern Ireland?
In England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, minor criminal offenses are handled in the Magistrates' Court, which does not use a jury.
What did the Scottish John Logie Baird develop?
John Logie Baird, a Scottish engineer, was a key pioneer who developed early electromechanical television systems in the 1920s.

name: British Citizenship Test 3
questions: Which of the following is a fundamental principle of British life?
Fundamental principles of British life include democracy, individual liberty, the rule of law, and mutual respect and tolerance.
Wales has its own established church.
Wales does not have an established state church. The Church in Wales was disestablished in 1920.
How is New Year’s Eve called in Scotland?
Hogmanay is the traditional Scottish word for New Year's Eve, celebrated with unique customs such as 'first-footing'.
Why did Henry VIII establish the church of England?
Because the Pope didn’t let him divorce his first wife, Catherine of Aragon
Because the Pope didn’t let him marry Catherine Howard
Because the Pope wanted England to be a Catholic country
Because the Pope didn’t let him divorce his wife, Anne of Cleves
Because the Pope didn’t let him divorce his first wife, Catherine of Aragon
King Henry VIII broke away from Rome and formed the Church of England in the 1530s because the Pope refused to grant him an annulment/divorce from Catherine of Aragon.
What is the name of the long war that English kings fought with France in the middle ages?
The Hundred Years War (1337-1453) was a series of connected conflicts fought between the rulers of England and France for dynastic control.
Who was supported by clansmen from the Scottish highlands and raised and army in 1745?
Prince Charles Edward Stuart (known as Bonnie Prince Charlie) led the Jacobite rising of 1745, backed by Scottish Highland clans, but was defeated at Culloden.
If you think someone is trying to persuade you to join an extremist or terrorist activity, who should you contact?
If you suspect extremist, radicalizing, or terrorist activities, you should report it to your local police force.
It is compulsory for 16 and 17-year-olds to join the National Citizen Service programme.
The National Citizen Service (NCS) is an exciting personal development opportunity, but it is purely voluntary, not compulsory.
What is the name of the tour guides that tell visitors stories about the Tower of London’s history?
Yeoman Warders (popularly known as 'Beefeaters') are historical guardians of the Tower of London who conduct tours for millions of visitors.
Which two countries developed the Concorde, the world’s only supersonic commercial airliner?
Concorde, the landmark commercial supersonic passenger jet airliner, was jointly developed and produced by aerospace teams in Britain and France.
Snowdonia National Park, containing Wales' highest peak (Yr Wyddfa / Mount Snowdon), is located in north-west Wales.
The famed detective Sherlock Holmes was created by Scottish physician and author Sir Arthur Conan Doyle in 1887.
Which country was invaded by Germany in 1939?
The German invasion of Poland on 1st September 1939 prompted Great Britain and France to declare war, marking the start of World War II.
Who is the patron Saint of Wales?
St David (Dewi Sant) is the patron saint of Wales, and is celebrated on St David's Day (1st March) every year.
Lake District is the largest national park of England.
The Lake District in Cumbria is England's largest and most famous National Park.
What is the name of the area in London where famous theatres are located?
The major theatrical district in London's West End is widely known as 'Theatreland'.
Which two of the following are key roles of school governors?
Setting the strategic direction of the school
Giving awards to the best students of the school
Monitoring and evaluating school performance; Setting the strategic direction of the school
School governors have key roles, which include setting strategic direction, and monitoring school performance.
What led the American colonies to want their independence from Britain?
The British government wanted to control their borders
They were running out of resources
The British government wanted to tax them
There were not enough jobs for the local people
The British government wanted to tax them
The American colonies rebelled against British taxation, giving rise to the famous slogan 'no taxation without representation'.
When did the Black Death take place?
The Black Death (bubonic plague) ravaged England, Wales, and Scotland during the late Middle Ages in 1348.
Who was the leader of the suffragettes, the group that campaigned for women’s rights to vote?
Emmeline Pankhurst founded the Women's Social and Political Union (WSPU) in 1903, leading the Suffragettes campaign for votes.
Cardiff is the capital city of which country?
Cardiff was officially designated as the capital city of Wales in 1955.
During the Great Depression in the 1930s which industry was badly affected?
Heavy industrial sectors such as shipbuilding and coal mining were devastated in Northern England and Scotland during the Great Depression.
Who was the first man in the world to run 1 mile in under 4 minutes?
Sir Roger Bannister was the first athlete to run a mile in under 4 minutes (3 minutes 59.4 seconds) in Oxford, 1954.
Which festival celebrates the end of Ramadan, when Muslims have fasted for a month?
Eid al-Fitr is the major Islamic festival that celebrates the conclusion of the holy month of fasting (Ramadan).

name: British Citizenship Test 4
questions: What was the last battle between Great Britain and France?
The Battle of Waterloo in 1815 was the definitive final battle between Napoleonic France and Great Britain (led by the Duke of Wellington).
Which flower is associated with Wales?
The daffodil and the leek are traditional national floral symbols associated with Wales.
During the reign of Charles II parts of London were destroyed, what was the cause of this destruction?
The Great Fire of London in 1666, during the reign of King Charles II, destroyed much of the medieval city of London, including Old St Paul's.
How often are general elections held in the UK?
General elections in the UK must take place at least once every 5 years under parliamentary law.
Scotland has its own banknotes, which are valid everywhere in the UK.
Scotland issues its own legal banknotes, which can be spent anywhere across the United Kingdom.
What charity works to preserve important buildings, coastline and countryside in the UK?
The National Trust is a major charity dedicated to preserving historic houses, natural coastlines, and pristine countryside throughout England, Wales, and Northern Ireland.
Great Britain refers only to England, Wales and Scotland.
'Great Britain' refers exclusively to the landmass consisting of England, Wales, and Scotland. It does not include Northern Ireland.
Who was the tribal leader who fought against the Romans?
Boudicca was the famous queen of the Iceni tribe of eastern Britain who led a massive uprising against Roman occupation in 60 AD.
Who was voted the greatest Briton of all time in 2002?
In 2002, Sir Winston Churchill was voted the greatest Briton of all time in a nationwide, televised BBC public poll.
Which two houses form the UK Parliament?
The House of Lords; House of Commons
The UK Parliament is bicameral, composed of the House of Commons (elected members) and the House of Lords (unelected peers).
When did women get the right to vote at the same age as men?
Equal voting rights for both genders (allowing everyone over 21 to vote) were established in 1928.
Who is the head of the Church of England?
The British monarch holds the title of Supreme Governor of the established Church of England.
What sort of event is the Grand National?
The Grand National is a historic and world-famous National Hunt horse race held annually at Aintree near Liverpool.
What type of literature are the Canterbury Tales?
The Canterbury Tales, written by Geoffrey Chaucer in Middle English, is a collection of poems and stories told by pilgrims.
Christmas Day, which celebrates the birth of Jesus Christ, is celebrated on 25th December.
Who supported King Charles I during the Civil War?
During the English Civil War (1642-1651), those who supported the King were called 'Cavaliers', while parliamentary supporters were called 'Roundheads'.
What battle is commemorated in the Bayeux Tapestry?
The Bayeux Tapestry is a historic medieval embroidery depicting the events leading up to the Norman conquest of England and the Battle of Hastings in 1066.
Where was Anne Boleyn, the wife of Henry VIII, executed?
Anne Boleyn, the second wife of King Henry VIII, was executed at the Tower of London in 1536.
Racial crime and smoking in public places are examples of:
Acts like racial hatred crime and smoking in public spaces are breaches of the public penal code, classified as criminal offenses.
What type of character was played by Charlie Chaplin?
Charlie Chaplin achieved global fame in silent movies, most famously playing his iconic, beloved character 'The Tramp'.
You have to be at least 21 years old to stand as MP.
To stand as an MP in the UK, you must be at least 18 years of age (reduced from 21 in 2006).
Sir Robert Watson-Watt developed early practical radar systems, which played an incredibly critical defensive role in the Battle of Britain.
Where is the official home of the Prime Minister?
10 Downing Street in London is the official workplace and primary residence of the British Prime Minister.
By law, which TWO types of media have to give a balanced coverage of all political parties and equal time to rival viewpoints before an election?
Broadcasting media (TV and radio) are strictly bound to give balanced, equal time coverage to major political parties before elections.

name: British Citizenship Test 5
questions: Easter, celebrating the resurrection of Christ, occurs on a variable Sunday in late March or April.
Which of the following is not a valid UK coin?
There is no active 25p coin in regular UK decimal circulation. Standard coins are 1p, 2p, 5p, 10p, 20p, 50p, £1, and £2.
Where is the Eden Project located?
The Eden Project, featuring massive biome greenhouses mimicking rainforest and Mediterranean climates, is situated in Cornwall.
St Helena and the Falkland Islands are part of Great Britain.
St Helena and the Falklands are British overseas territories, but they are geographically distant and not part of Great Britain itself.
Which two of the following are fundamental principles of British life?
The core principles of British life are: Democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect.
Where should you register if you want to become part of a jury?
Juries are compiled by randomly selecting individuals who are registered on the local electoral register.
What sort of church is the Church of Scotland?
The Church of Scotland (known as the Kirk) is a Presbyterian church and the established national church of Scotland.
Scotland is widely known as the home and origin of modern golf, with historic records of play going back to the 15th century.
When do the television and newspapers have stories that are jokes until midday?
April Fool's Day (1st April) is a traditional day for play pranks and practical jokes, which must stop at midday by custom.
What king was defeated by Oliver Cromwell during the Civil War and hid in an oak tree before escaping to Europe?
Following defeat at the Battle of Worcester in 1651, Charles II famously escaped capture by hiding in a hollow royal oak tree.
Who was the father of Queen Elizabeth I?
Henry VIII was the father of Queen Elizabeth I (whose mother was Anne Boleyn).
Complaints against the police can ONLY be made by writing to the Police Complaints Commissioner.
You can make a complaint against the police at any local police station or by writing to the Chief Constable, not only to a single Commissioner.
Who is the patron Saint of Northern Ireland?
St Patrick is the patron saint of Northern Ireland. His feast day is celebrated on 17th March.
What is the name of the period when new ideas about politics, philosophy and science were developed?
The Enlightenment was an 18th-century intellectual movement promoting rational scientific thought, philosophy, and political reform.
Which of the following statements is TRUE:
Mary Stuart (‘Mary, Queen of Scots’) was a Protestant
Mary Stuart (‘Mary, Queen of Scots’) was a Catholic
Mary Stuart (‘Mary, Queen of Scots’) was a Catholic
Mary Stuart, Queen of Scots, was a devout Catholic whose religion brought her into direct conflict with Protestant lords and her cousin Elizabeth I.
Which of the following is an example of civil law?
To sell tobacco products to anyone under the age of 18
To buy alcohol for people who are under the age of 18
To carry a weapon of any kind, even if it is for self-defence
Civil law deals with private disputes, such as workplace discrimination, whereas selling weapons, under-age sales, and violent assaults fall under criminal law.
In which battle did Admiral Nelson die?
Admiral Horatio Nelson was fatally wounded during the historic British naval victory at the Battle of Trafalgar in 1805.

William of Orange was asked by Protestants to invade England and proclaim himself king. But, when William reached England, there was no resistance and he took over the throne. This event was later known as:
The 1688 bloodless takeover of the throne from James II by William of Orange and Queen Mary is celebrated as the Glorious Revolution.
What sort of charity is ‘Friends of the Earth’?
A charity working with older people
'Friends of the Earth' is a prominent international non-governmental environmental campaign group.
If a husband forces his wife to have sex he can be charged with rape.
In 1991, marital rape was officially recognized as illegal under UK law, establishing that consent must always be given.
In which country of the British Empire did the Boer War (1899-1902) take place?
The Boer War (1899-1902) was fought between British forces and Dutch settlers (Boers) in South Africa.
Which of the following actions is known as “canvassing”?
Caring for animals at a local rescue shelter
Persuading people to vote for a political party
Persuading people to vote for a political party
Canvassing refers to political campaign workers speaking directly with voters to persuade them to support a candidate or party.
Which novel written by JRR Tolkien was voted the country’s best-loved novel in 2003?
J.R.R. Tolkien's masterpiece 'The Lord of the Rings' was voted the country's best-loved novel in the BBC's 2003 'Big Read' poll.
Germany launched its invasion of Poland on 1st September 1939, triggering the start of the Second World War.

name: British Citizenship Test 6
questions: As a British citizen what are your responsibilities (choose two answers)?
To respect and obey the law
To walk your dog only during the day
To go to church on Sunday
To look after yourself and your family
To respect and obey the law; To look after yourself and your family
Under the official guidelines, key responsibilities include respecting laws and looking after your family.
Who made the first coins to be minted in Britain?
The people of the Stone Age
The people of the Iron Age
The people of the Iron Age
The first coins to be minted in Britain were introduced by Iron Age communities in the first century BC.
Who built the Tower of London?
The majestic White Tower (the central keep of the Tower of London) was built by William the Conqueror to dominate Londoners.
There are 15 national parks in England, Wales and Scotland. What are national parks?
Land formations of columns made from volcanic lava
National parks in the UK are designated regions of protected countryside where development is strictly controlled.
Northern Ireland has its own established church.
Northern Ireland does not have an established state church.
Which three territories form Great Britain?
Great Britain consists of England, Scotland, and Wales. Adding Northern Ireland forms the 'United Kingdom'.
How often are ’Prime Minister’s Questions’ held in the parliament?
Prime Minister's Questions (PMQs) are held every Wednesday noon when Parliament is sitting.
King Charles I was executed outside Whitehall Banqueting House in January 1649 following his defeat in the civil war.
William Shakespeare was born in 1564 in the market town of Stratford-upon-Avon in Warwickshire.
Which two of the following are famous British Paralympians?
Tanni Grey-Thompson and Ellie Simmonds are world-famous British Paralympic athletes.
Who was reigning in England when English settlers first began to colonise the eastern coast of America?
English colonization in North America began during the late Elizabethan era, notably with Sir Walter Raleigh's attempts.
Scotland and Wales use a system called ‘individual registration’ where all those entitled to vote must complete their own registration form.
Individual registration was introduced to replace household registration across the whole UK, not just Scotland and Wales.
On what day is the birth of Jesus Christ celebrated?
Christmas Day celebrates the birth of Jesus Christ, celebrated globally on 25th December.
What sort of battle was the ’Battle of Britain’, fought between Germany and Britain in the summer of 1940?
The Battle of Britain was a crucial aerial battle in 1940 between the German Luftwaffe and the British RAF.
Swansea is a major coastal city and county in south Wales.
Which two political parties formed a coalition in 2010?
The Conservative Party; The Liberal Democrats Party
Following the 2010 general election, the Conservatives and Liberal Democrats formed a coalition government with David Cameron as PM.
Who established the Church of England?
Henry VIII established the independent Church of England as part of his split from the Roman Catholic Church.
In 1348, one third of the population in England, Wales and Scotland died as a result of which disease?
In 1348, the devastating Black Death plague swept through Great Britain, killing about one-third of the population.
Haggis is a traditional food from which area?
Haggis is a historic and highly celebrated traditional savory pudding dish from Scotland.
Which court deals with minor criminal offences in Scotland?
The Justice of the Peace Court
The Justice of the Peace Court
In Scotland, minor criminal cases are dealt with in the Justice of the Peace Court.
Which two of the following records give us information about England during the reign of William I?
The Domesday Book; The Bayeux Tapestry
The Domesday Book and Bayeux Tapestry are vital historic artifacts recording England under William the Conqueror.
In 1913, the British government promised ‘Home Rule’ for Ireland, why were changes in Ireland delayed until 1921?
Due to the outbreak of the First World War
Due to the outbreak of the Second World War
Because there was not a king on the British throne
Due to the outbreak of the Black Death
Due to the outbreak of the First World War
Irish Home Rule was suspended due to the outbreak of World War I in 1914, postponing political settlements.
Which of the following statements is true:
Elizabeth I was a Protestant and she succeeded in finding a balance between the views of the Catholics and the more extreme Protestants.
Elizabeth I was a Catholic and she succeeded in finding a balance between the views of the Catholics and the more extreme Protestants.
Elizabeth I was a Protestant and she succeeded in finding a balance between the views of the Catholics and the more extreme Protestants.
Queen Elizabeth I established a moderate Protestant religious settlement to reconcile split Catholic and radical Protestant views.
Which two documents do you need to apply for a National Insurance number?
A document with your address on it, such as a tenancy agreement
Documents that prove that you have permission to work in the UK
Documents that prove that you have permission to work in the UK; Documents that prove your identity
To apply for a National Insurance Number, you need documents proving identity and UK work permissions.

name: British Citizenship Test 7
questions: As a British citizen, you should:
Look after the area in which you live and the environment
Respect and obey the law; Look after the area in which you live and the environment
British citizens should respect and obey the law, and look after the local area and environment.
Halloween is a pagan-originated festival celebrated annually on the evening of 31st October.
The Bill of Rights in 1689 gave women the right to vote.
The 1689 Bill of Rights did not grant votes to women, which only occurred starting from the early 20th century.
What is the name of the most famous cricket competition played between England and Australia?
The Ashes is the historic and famous test cricket series contested biennially between England and Australia.
What was the biggest source of employment during the 18th century?
During the Industrial Revolution in the 18th century, manufacturing in factories quickly overtook agriculture as the largest source of work.
In 1314 the Scottish, led by Robert the Bruce, defeated the English at the battle of Bannockburn, and Scotland remained unconquered by the English.
At the Battle of Bannockburn in 1314, Robert the Bruce successfully secured Scotland's independence from English rule.
Which of the following is an example of criminal offence?
Smoking in public places where it is not allowed
Disputes about faulty goods or services
Disputes about an unfair dismissal in the workplace
A dispute between the landlord and the tenants who have not paid the rent
Smoking in public places where it is not allowed
Smoking in enclosed public places is a criminal offense in the UK, whereas contractual or tenancy disputes are civil matters.
Which Scottish clan was killed for not taking the oath?
In the Glencoe Massacre of 1692, members of the MacDonald clan were famously murdered for delayed oath of allegiance to William III.
Which two issues can the devolved administrations pass laws on?
Devolved administrations deal with local policy matters like healthcare and education. Foreign policy and defense remain 'reserved' to Westminister.
The assassination of the Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria in 1914 led to which of the following wars?
The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in June 1914 was the diplomatic trigger for the outbreak of World War I.
What is the capital city of Scotland?
Edinburgh is the capital city of Scotland, hosting the devolved Scottish Parliament.
In 1833 the Emancipation Act abolished slavery throughout the British Empire.
The Slavery Abolition Act 1833 (known as the Emancipation Act) prohibited slavery across almost all components of the British Empire.
What is the name of the process by which many Scottish landlords destroyed individual small farms (known as ‘crofts’) to make space for large flocks of sheep and cattle?
The Highland Clearances occurred in 18th/19th century Scotland when landlords forcibly evicted farmers to run profitable sheep-farming operations.
The Falkland Islands are a British overseas territory and are part of the United Kingdom.
The Falkland Islands are a British overseas territory, but they do not form part of the United Kingdom.
Which two of the following are Civil War Battles?
The Battle of Marston Moor; The Battle of Naseby
Marston Moor (1644) and Naseby (1645) were key Parliamentary victories during the English Civil War.
What was the name of the activist group who fought for the women‘s right to vote?
The Suffragettes were members of the late-19th/early-20th century movement who campaigned for women's suffrage using civil disobedience.
What UK landmark was voted as Britain’s favourite view in 2007?
In 2007, an ITV poll voted Wastwater in the Lake District National Park as 'Britain's Favourite View'.
Who were the first people to live in Britain in what we call the Stone Age?
The earliest people in Britain during the Stone Age lived mobile lives as hunter-gatherers, following herds of wild animals.
What is the name of the movement against the authority of the Pope and the ideas of the Catholic Church that took place during the reign of Henry VIII?
The Reformation challenged the Pope's authority and shifted England's religious identity to Protestantism.
What do you need to do to apply for a National Insurance Number?
Contact the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP)
Ask you employer to get it for you
Contact the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP)
To obtain or apply for a National Insurance Number, you must contact the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP).
Which of the following is a major horse-racing event in England?
Royal Ascot is a highly popular, historic five-day horse racing meeting attended by the Royal Family in Berkshire.
How many members form a jury in Scotland?
Scottish criminal trials require a panel of 15 jurors (unlike 12 in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland) and can reach three verdicts: guilty, not guilty, or not proven.
Lent refers to the forty days of penitence and reflection in Christian tradition leading directly up to Easter.
When was the last successful foreign invasion of England?
The Norman Invasion of 1066 was the last successful military invasion and conquest of England.

name: British Citizenship Test 8
questions: World War II started as a result of Germany invading which country?
World War II was triggered on 3rd September 1939 after Germany invaded Poland, which had defensive pacts with France and Britain.
Which flower is associated with Scotland?
The prickly purple thistle has been a recognized national symbol of Scotland since the reign of Alexander III.
